name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q01 - Fundamentals of plant growth, meristems, and measurement

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding plant growth:

Statement I: Growth is an irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ, its parts, or even an individual cell.

Statement II: Root apical meristem and shoot apical meristem are responsible for primary growth and elongation of plants along their axis.

Statement III: Cells in the meristematic phase have thin, primary cellulosic cell walls with abundant plasmodesmatal connections.

Statement IV: The growth of a pollen tube is measured in terms of its length, whereas an increase in surface area denotes growth in a dorsiventral leaf.

Statement V: Lateral meristems such as vascular cambium and cork-cambium are responsible for primary growth in monocotyledonous plants.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant growth is an irreversible increase in size driven by primary and secondary meristems and quantified using organ-appropriate parameters.

Step 2: Evaluation of Definition, Apical Meristems, and Meristematic Cell Walls
The claim defining growth as an irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ, its parts, or an individual cell is accurate. The claim that root and shoot apical meristems drive primary growth and axial elongation is accurate. The claim that meristematic phase cells possess thin, primary cellulosic cell walls with abundant plasmodesmatal connections is also accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Measurement Parameters
The claim that pollen tube growth is measured in terms of length while dorsiventral leaf growth is measured as an increase in surface area is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Lateral Meristems
The claim that vascular cambium and cork-cambium cause primary growth in monocotyledonous plants is incorrect. Lateral meristems (vascular cambium and cork-cambium) appear later in life in dicotyledonous plants and gymnosperms and cause secondary growth (increase in girth).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Four of the five biological claims (growth definition, apical meristem primary growth, meristematic wall structure, and pollen tube/leaf growth parameters) are correct, while the claim regarding lateral meristems in monocots is incorrect. Hence, only four statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q02 - Growth rates, differentiation, dedifferentiation, and plasticity

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding growth rates, differentiation, and plasticity:

Statement I: In arithmetic growth, only one daughter cell continues to divide after mitosis while the other differentiates and matures, yielding a linear curve \(L_t = L_0 + rt\).

Statement II: In geometric growth, both progeny cells retain the ability to divide, and under limited nutrient supply, growth slows down to produce a sigmoid curve.

Statement III: Living differentiated cells that have lost the capacity to divide can regain it under certain conditions through dedifferentiation, as seen in interfascicular cambium formation.

Statement IV: Heterophylly in cotton, coriander, and larkspur represents plasticity between juvenile and mature phases of the plant.

Statement V: During differentiation to form a tracheary element, cells retain their protoplasm and develop thin, primary cellulosic walls.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant growth kinetics follow arithmetic or geometric patterns, while cellular maturation involves differentiation, dedifferentiation, and developmental plasticity.

Step 2: Evaluation of Arithmetic and Geometric Growth
The claim that arithmetic growth involves one continuously dividing daughter cell and follows the linear equation \(L_t = L_0 + rt\) is accurate. The claim that geometric growth involves both progeny cells dividing and forms a sigmoid curve under limited nutrients is also accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Dedifferentiation and Plasticity
The claim that living differentiated parenchyma cells regain division capacity to form interfascicular cambium via dedifferentiation is accurate. The claim that heterophylly in cotton, coriander, and larkspur reflects plasticity between juvenile and mature phases is also accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Tracheary Element Differentiation
The claim that cells forming a tracheary element retain their protoplasm and develop thin, primary cellulosic walls is incorrect. To form a tracheary element, cells lose their protoplasm and develop very strong, elastic, lignocellulosic secondary cell walls to transport water over long distances under extreme tension.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding arithmetic growth, geometric sigmoid growth, dedifferentiation into interfascicular cambium, and developmental heterophylly are correct, whereas the claim regarding tracheary element wall and protoplasm structure is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q03 - Chemical nature and historical discovery of PGRs

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the chemical nature and discovery of plant growth regulators:

Statement I: Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) is an indole compound, while gibberellic acid (\(\text{GA}_3\)) is a terpene.

Statement II: Kinetin is an adenine derivative that was first crystallised by Miller et al. (1955) and occurs abundantly as a natural hormone in higher plants.

Statement III: Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin observed phototropism in canary grass coleoptiles, while F.W. Went isolated auxin from oat seedling coleoptile tips.

Statement IV: E. Kurosawa observed 'bakanae' disease symptoms in rice seedlings treated with sterile filtrates of Gibberella fujikuroi.

Statement V: Inhibitor-B, abscission II, and dormin were later proved to be chemically identical and named abscisic acid (ABA), a carotenoid derivative.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant growth regulators belong to diverse chemical groups and were discovered independently through experimental studies on tropism, fungal disease, tissue culture, and growth inhibition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Chemical Classes and Classic Discoveries
The claim that IAA is an indole compound and \(\text{GA}_3\) is a terpene is accurate. The claim that Charles and Francis Darwin observed phototropism in canary grass coleoptiles while F.W. Went isolated auxin from oat coleoptile tips is accurate. The claim that E. Kurosawa observed 'bakanae' symptoms using sterile filtrates of Gibberella fujikuroi is accurate. The claim that inhibitor-B, abscission II, and dormin were proved chemically identical as ABA, a carotenoid derivative, is also accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Natural Occurrence of Kinetin
The claim that kinetin occurs abundantly as a natural hormone in higher plants is incorrect. Although Miller et al. (1955) identified and crystallised kinetin (an adenine derivative), kinetin does not occur naturally in plants; natural cytokinins include zeatin.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Four of the five biological claims are accurate, while the claim stating that kinetin occurs naturally in higher plants is incorrect. Hence, only four statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q04 - Physiological effects of all five PGR groups

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the physiological effects of plant growth regulators:

Statement I: Synthetic auxin 2,4-D is widely used to kill dicotyledonous weeds without affecting mature monocotyledonous plants.

Statement II: Gibberellins delay senescence in fruits, speed up malting in the brewing industry, and promote bolting in rosette plants such as beet and cabbages.

Statement III: Ethylene promotes rapid internode or petiole elongation in deep water rice plants and breaks dormancy in peanut seeds and potato tubers.

Statement IV: Ethephon hastens fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples and promotes male flowers in cucumbers to increase yield.

Statement V: Abscisic acid (ABA) stimulates stomatal closure during stress and acts synergistically with gibberellins to promote seed germination.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each of the five PGR groups exerts specific physiological effects that can be promotive, inhibitory, or antagonistic depending on the plant tissue and developmental stage.

Step 2: Evaluation of Auxin, Gibberellin, and Ethylene Effects
The claim that 2,4-D selectively kills dicotyledonous weeds without affecting mature monocotyledonous plants is accurate. The claim that gibberellins delay fruit senescence, speed up malting, and promote bolting in beet and cabbages is accurate. The claim that ethylene promotes rapid internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice and breaks dormancy in peanut seeds and potato tubers is also accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Ethephon Effect in Cucumbers
The claim that ethephon promotes male flowers in cucumbers is incorrect; ethephon promotes female flowers in cucumbers, thereby increasing the yield.

Step 4: Evaluation of ABA Interaction with Gibberellins
The claim that ABA acts synergistically with gibberellins to promote seed germination is incorrect. While ABA stimulates stomatal closure during stress, it inhibits seed germination and acts as an antagonist to gibberellins in most physiological situations.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims concerning 2,4-D, gibberellin applications, and ethylene effects on deep water rice and dormancy breaking are correct, whereas the claims regarding male flowers in cucumbers and synergistic germination with ABA are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTH_MCQ_Q05 - Photoperiodism, vernalisation, and seed dormancy

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding photoperiodism, vernalisation, and seed dormancy:

Statement I: Long day plants require light exposure exceeding a critical duration to induce flowering, whereas short day plants require light exposure less than this critical duration.

Statement II: Flowering in photoperiodic plants depends not only on the duration of the light period, but the duration of the dark period is also of equal importance.

Statement III: Shoot apices themselves perceive photoperiods directly without any involvement of leaves.

Statement IV: Winter varieties of wheat, barley, and rye are planted in autumn so they overwinter as seedlings, resume growth in spring, and are harvested around mid-summer.

Statement V: Seed dormancy caused by hard seed coats or chemical inhibitors can be overcome by mechanical abrasions, chilling conditions, or application of gibberellic acid and nitrates.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Photoperiodism and vernalisation govern flowering in response to light/dark durations and low temperature, while seed dormancy is an endogenous block to germination that can be broken by physical or chemical treatments.

Step 2: Evaluation of Photoperiodism and Dark Period
The claim defining long day plants and short day plants relative to critical light duration is accurate. The claim that the duration of the dark period is of equal importance alongside the light period is also accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Site of Photoperiod Perception
The claim that shoot apices perceive photoperiods directly without leaf involvement is incorrect. Although shoot apices modify into flowering apices prior to flowering, they cannot perceive photoperiods by themselves; the site of perception of light/dark duration is the leaves, from which a hypothesised hormonal substance migrates to the shoot apices.

Step 4: Evaluation of Vernalisation and Seed Dormancy
The claim regarding autumn planting and mid-summer harvesting of winter varieties of wheat, barley, and rye is accurate. Likewise, the claim that seed dormancy from hard seed coats or chemical inhibitors can be overcome by mechanical abrasions, chilling, or gibberellic acid and nitrates is accurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Four of the five biological claims are accurate, whereas the claim that shoot apices directly perceive photoperiods without leaves is incorrect. Hence, only four statements are correct.
